title: Elon Musk Predictions & Outcomes: 2019 to 2026
summary: Explore Elon Musk's Tesla predictions and see which came true by 2026, including FSD progress and Optimus outcomes.
body_text: In honour of Tesla earnings, here is a list of predictions and promises made by Elon Musk from 2019 to now. We've included an indicator of which were achieved, which weren't and the eventual date of the outcome, if any. View in platform here to filter by topic, sort by date etc. Coverage window: Feb 19, 2019 to 2026-05-18 — 151 public predictions by Elon Musk about Tesla, assessed as of 2026-07-16. "Result" = whether the prediction came true by its predicted deadline (No / Yes / Yes (qualified) / Partly / Unresolved / Not yet assessable). Date Topic Prediction Predicted Deadline Result Outcome Date Assessment Notes Type Venue Prediction Sources Evidence Sources 2019-02-19 Autonomy / FSD Tesla would be feature-complete on full self-driving in 2019. 2019-12-31 No Tesla did not reach feature-complete full autonomy in 2019. Tesla still describes FSD as supervised and as not making the vehicle autonomous; NHTSA records Tesla's characterization of it as SAE Level 2. Feature-complete was Musk's term; outcome judged against unsupervised autonomy, not driver-assistance feature availability. Interview ARK Invest podcast wired.com ; Tesla, Inc., Q3 2019 Earnings Call (Oct. 23, 2019) tesla.com ; nhtsa.gov 2019-02-19 Autonomy / FSD By the end of 2020, a driver would be able to fall asleep and wake up at the destination. 2020-12-31 No The capability was not available by the end of 2020 and remains inconsistent with Tesla's current requirement for an attentive driver and active supervision. This is a concrete hands-off/sleeping-capable autonomy forecast. Interview ARK Invest podcast wired.com ; Tesla, Inc., Q1 2020 Earnings Call (Apr. 29, 2020) tesla.com ; nhtsa.gov 2019-02-19 Vehicle deliveries Tesla will make around 500,000 cars in 2019. 2019-12-31 No 2019-12-31 Tesla delivered 367,500 vehicles in 2019 and produced about 365,300, well below 500,000. Musk corrected the tweet hours later, but the original prediction itself did not come true. Original tweet assessed separately from the later correction. Tweet X / Twitter x.com ; wired.com sec.gov ; theguardian.com 2019-02-20 Vehicle production rate Tesla's annualized production rate would probably be around 500,000 vehicles at the end of 2019. 2019-12-31 No 2019-12-31 Tesla produced 104,891 vehicles in Q4 2019, an annualized rate of about 419,600, below 500,000. Annualized rate is calculated as four times Tesla's reported Q4 production. Tweet correction X / Twitter wired.com ; theguardian.com sec.gov 2019-02-20 Vehicle deliveries Tesla would deliver about 400,000 vehicles in 2019. 2019-12-31 No 2019-12-31 Tesla delivered 367,500 vehicles in 2019, about 8.1% below the corrected 400,000 forecast. Corrected delivery forecast assessed separately from the original 500,000 tweet. Tweet correction X / Twitter wired.com ; theguardian.com sec.gov 2019-04-22 Autonomy / FSD Tesla would have a no-touch, human-intervention-free self-driving system by the second quarter of 2020. 2020-06-30 No Tesla did not release unsupervised, intervention-free FSD by Q2 2020; its current FSD remains supervised and SAE Level 2. Deadline taken from the Autonomy Day presentation. Public presentation Tesla Autonomy Day youtube.com ; cbsnews.com tesla.com ; nhtsa.gov 2019-04-22 Robotaxi Tesla would have one million robotaxis on the road in 2020. 2020-12-31 No Tesla had no commercial robotaxi network in 2020. Its first limited paid robotaxi rides began in Austin on June 22, 2025 with about ten vehicles and a front-seat safety monitor. A limited 2025 pilot does not satisfy a one-million-vehicle 2020 forecast. Public presentation Tesla Autonomy Day youtube.com ; techcrunch.com reuters.com ; reuters.com 2019-04-24 Tesla Insurance Tesla hoped to launch its insurance product in about one month. 2019-05-24 No 2019-08-28 Tesla Insurance launched in California in late August 2019, roughly three months after the one-month window. Deadline normalized to one month after the call. Earnings call Tesla Q1 2019 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q1 2019 Earnings Call (Apr. 24, 2019) tesla.com 2019-04-24 Energy storage Powerwall and Powerpack deployments could grow by roughly 300% in 2019. 2019-12-31 No Tesla reported 1.65 GWh of storage deployments in 2019 versus 1.04 GWh in 2018, an increase of about 59%, not 300%. Assessed using energy-storage capacity deployed, Tesla's reported company-wide metric. Earnings call Tesla Q1 2019 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q1 2019 Earnings Call (Apr. 24, 2019) sec.gov 2019-04-24 Battery technology event Tesla would probably hold a battery and cell investor day later in 2019 or early in 2020. 2020-03-31 No 2020-09-22 Tesla's Battery Day was held on September 22, 2020, after the stated window. Early 2020' normalized to the end of Q1. Earnings call Tesla Q1 2019 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q1 2019 Earnings Call (Apr. 24, 2019) tesla.com 2019-05-09 Autonomy / FSD A Tesla would drive from Los Angeles to New York with no human intervention by the end of 2019. 2019-12-31 No No such intervention-free cross-country Tesla trip occurred by the deadline. Tesla's production FSD still requires active driver supervision. The tweet revived and generalized an earlier cross-country promise. Tweet X / Twitter x.com ; autopilotreview.com tesla.com ; nhtsa.gov 2019-07-24 Gigafactory Shanghai Gigafactory Shanghai would be producing Model 3s in volume by the end of 2019. 2019-12-31 Yes 2019-12-31 Tesla reported that Shanghai had begun trial production in Q4 2019 and had demonstrated a production run-rate above 3,000 vehicles per week before year-end. Earnings call Tesla Q2 2019 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q2 2019 Earnings Call (Jul. 24, 2019) ir.tesla.com ; sec.gov 2019-07-24 Profitability Tesla expected to be around breakeven in Q3 2019 and profitable in Q4 2019. 2019-12-31 Yes 2019-12-31 Tesla reported positive GAAP net income attributable to common stockholders in both Q3 and Q4 2019, satisfying the breakeven/profitability forecast. Earnings call Tesla Q2 2019 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q2 2019 Earnings Call (Jul. 24, 2019) ir.tesla.com ; ir.tesla.com 2019-07-24 Gigafactory location Tesla would finalize and announce its European Gigafactory location before the end of 2019. 2019-12-31 Yes 2019-11-12 Musk announced Berlin as the European Gigafactory location on November 12, 2019. Earnings call Tesla Q2 2019 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q2 2019 Earnings Call (Jul. 24, 2019) reuters.com ; tesla.com 2019-07-24 Battery technology event Tesla's battery technology event would probably take place in February or March 2020. 2020-03-31 No 2020-09-22 Tesla held Battery Day on September 22, 2020, about six months after the stated window. A more specific revision of the Q1 2019 event forecast; retained because the deadline changed. Earnings call Tesla Q2 2019 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q2 2019 Earnings Call (Jul. 24, 2019) tesla.com 2019-07-24 Gigafactory Berlin Tesla would probably have an operational European Gigafactory in 2021. 2021-12-31 No 2022-03-22 Tesla opened Gigafactory Berlin-Brandenburg and delivered the first vehicles in March 2022, after 2021. Earnings call Tesla Q2 2019 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q2 2019 Earnings Call (Jul. 24, 2019) bbc.com ; tesla.com 2019-10-23 Model Y Model Y production would begin by summer 2020. 2020-09-22 Yes 2020-01-29 Tesla reported that Model Y production began in January 2020 and deliveries started in March, several months before summer. Summer deadline normalized to the September equinox; production actually began much earlier. Earnings call Tesla Q3 2019 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q3 2019 Earnings Call (Oct. 23, 2019); businessinsider.com ir.tesla.com ; ir.tesla.com 2019-10-23 Model Y Tesla expected Model Y volume production above 1,000 vehicles per week no later than mid-2020. 2020-06-30 Unresolved Tesla began Model Y production and deliveries in early 2020, but its public Q2 reporting combined Model 3 and Model Y output, so the specific 1,000-per-week threshold by June cannot be independently verified. Kept separate from the existing Model Y start-date forecast because this forecast specified a volume threshold. Earnings call Tesla Q3 2019 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q3 2019 Earnings Call (Oct. 23, 2019) ir.tesla.com ; sec.gov 2019-11-21 Cybertruck Cybertruck production would start in late 2021. 2021-12-31 No 2023-11-30 Customer deliveries began at a November 30, 2023 delivery event, roughly two years late. Late fulfillment is recorded as No because the requested test is within the predicted timeline. Product unveiling Cybertruck reveal theverge.com ; Tesla, Inc., Q3 2020 Earnings Call (Oct. 21, 2020); Tesla, Inc., Q4 2020 Earnings Call (Jan. 27, 2021) tesla.com ; wired.com 2019-11-21 Cybertruck The base Cybertruck would start at $39,900. 2023-11-30 No 2023-11-30 At the 2023 delivery event Tesla priced the least-expensive announced version at $60,990; the later offered Long Range version was also far above $39,900. Nominal prices; tax credits and incentives excluded. Product unveiling Cybertruck reveal greencarreports.com ; theverge.com wired.com ; reuters.com 2019-11-21 Cybertruck The tri-motor Cybertruck would have more than 500 miles of range. 2023-11-30 No 2023-11-30 Production Cybertruck versions announced at delivery had about 320 to 340 miles of estimated range, not 500-plus miles. Range-extender concepts that were not delivered are not counted. Product unveiling Cybertruck reveal greencarreports.com ; theverge.com wired.com ; tesla.com 2020-01-29 Vehicle deliveries Tesla should comfortably exceed 500,000 vehicle deliveries in 2020. 2020-12-31 No 2020-12-31 Tesla delivered 499,550 vehicles in 2020, 450 short of 500,000; therefore it did not literally exceed 500,000, let alone comfortably. Strict threshold assessment; the miss was only about 0.09%. Earnings call Tesla Q4 2019 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q4 2019 Earnings Call (Jan. 29, 2020); fool.com ir.tesla.com 2020-01-29 Autonomy / FSD Tesla would be feature-complete on Full Self-Driving in a couple of months. 2020-03-31 No Tesla did not deliver unsupervised feature-complete driving by March 2020; Tesla still describes FSD as supervised and not autonomous. A couple of months' normalized to March 31, 2020. This is a revised deadline, not a duplicate of the 2019 deadline. Earnings call Tesla Q4 2019 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q4 2019 Earnings Call (Jan. 29, 2020) tesla.com ; nhtsa.gov 2020-01-29 Battery technology event Tesla's Battery Day would probably be in April 2020. 2020-04-30 No 2020-09-22 Battery Day occurred on September 22, 2020. A later, more specific deadline revision. Earnings call Tesla Q4 2019 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q4 2019 Earnings Call (Jan. 29, 2020) tesla.com 2020-01-29 Model S Plaid Tesla expected the Plaid powertrain and vehicle to be available by the end of 2020. 2020-12-31 No 2021-06-10 Tesla delivered the first Model S Plaid vehicles in June 2021. Earnings call Tesla Q4 2019 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q4 2019 Earnings Call (Jan. 29, 2020) reuters.com 2020-04-12 Robotaxi Robotaxi functionality would still be ready in 2020, subject to regulatory approval. 2020-12-31 No No Tesla robotaxi functionality capable of commercial driverless service was delivered in 2020; FSD remained supervised. Regulatory approval was not the only missing condition; technical supervision remained required. Tweet X / Twitter caranddriver.com ; Tesla, Inc., Q3 2019 Earnings Call (Oct. 23, 2019) tesla.com ; nhtsa.gov 2020-04-29 FSD subscription Tesla would release an FSD subscription option by the end of 2020. 2020-12-31 No 2021-07-17 Tesla launched the monthly FSD subscription in July 2021. Earnings call Tesla Q1 2020 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q1 2020 Earnings Call (Apr. 29, 2020) theverge.com 2020-04-29 Gigafactory location Tesla would announce its next U.S. Gigafactory location within one to three months. 2020-07-29 Yes 2020-07-22 Tesla announced Austin, Texas, as the location of its next Gigafactory on July 22, 2020, within three months of the call. Deadline is three months after the call, the outer edge of the stated range. Earnings call Tesla Q1 2020 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q1 2020 Earnings Call (Apr. 29, 2020) cnbc.com 2020-04-29 Solar Roof Tesla aimed to install 1,000 Solar Roofs per week by the end of 2020. 2020-12-31 No Wood Mackenzie estimated only about 3,000 Solar Roof installations in total through early 2023, with the best quarter averaging roughly 32 systems per week, far below 1,000 per week. Earnings call Tesla Q1 2020 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q1 2020 Earnings Call (Apr. 29, 2020) woodmac.com ; sec.gov 2020-04-29 Robotaxi Tesla could deploy robotaxis in some markets in 2021, subject to regulatory approval. 2021-12-31 No 2025-06-22 Tesla did not operate a driverless commercial robotaxi service in any market in 2021; its first limited paid Austin robotaxi service began in June 2025. Earnings call Tesla Q1 2020 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q1 2020 Earnings Call (Apr. 29, 2020) reuters.com ; tesla.com 2020-07-09 Autonomy / FSD Tesla was very close to Level 5 and would have the basic functionality complete in 2020. 2020-12-31 No Tesla did not achieve Level 5 or complete its basic functionality in 2020. Current FSD remains supervised and Tesla characterizes it as SAE Level 2. Level 5 means full automation under all driving conditions. Video address World Artificial Intelligence Conference reuters.com ; Tesla, Inc., Q2 2020 Earnings Call (Jul. 22, 2020) tesla.com ; nhtsa.gov 2020-09-22 Affordable vehicle Battery advances would enable a compelling $25,000 fully autonomous Tesla in about three years. 2023-09-22 No Tesla had not launched a $25,000 car by September 2023 or by the assessment date. Even Tesla's lower-priced 2025 Model 3 and Model Y variants were roughly $36,990 and $39,990 before incentives, and FSD remained supervised. Three years measured from Battery Day. Public presentation Tesla Battery Day tesla.com ; greencarreports.com assets-ir.tesla.com ; tesla.com 2020-09-22 Battery production Tesla aimed to reach 3 terawatt-hours per year of battery-cell production by 2030. 2030-12-31 Not yet assessable The 2030 deadline has not arrived. This row records the forecast but does not score present capacity as a failure before the deadline. Aspirational production target with an explicit date; included because it is measurable. Public presentation Tesla Battery Day tesla.com ; rev.com tesla.com ; assets-ir.tesla.com 2020-09-22 Vehicle production Tesla would probably produce 20 million vehicles per year before 2030. 2029-12-31 Not yet assessable The deadline has not arrived. Tesla delivered 1.64 million vehicles in 2025, so reaching 20 million annually would require a very large later ramp, but early scoring would be inappropriate. Before 2030' normalized to December 31, 2029. Public presentation Tesla Battery Day businessinsider.com ; tesla.com assets-ir.tesla.com ; tesla.com 2020-10-12 Autonomy / FSD Tesla would release a limited FSD beta on Tuesday, October 20, 2020. 2020-10-20 Yes 2020-10-20 Tesla began the limited FSD beta release on October 20, 2020, matching the stated day. This predicts a beta release, not autonomous capability. Tweet X / Twitter engadget.com ; teslarati.com x.com ; theverge.com 2020-10-21 Gigafactory Berlin and Texas Tesla expected Gigafactory Berlin and Gigafactory Texas to produce and deliver vehicles in 2021. 2021-12-31 No 2022-04-07 Customer deliveries from both factories began in 2022: Berlin in March and Texas in April. The same forecast was repeated on the Q4 2020 call and is consolidated here. Earnings call Tesla Q3 2020 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q3 2020 Earnings Call (Oct. 21, 2020) bbc.com ; tesla.com 2020-10-21 Energy storage Tesla expected energy-storage deployments to roughly double in 2021. 2021-12-31 No Tesla's storage deployments rose from about 3.0 GWh in 2020 to 4.0 GWh in 2021, roughly 32%, not 100%. Earnings call Tesla Q3 2020 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q3 2020 Earnings Call (Oct. 21, 2020) sec.gov ; sec.gov 2021-01-27 Autonomy / FSD Tesla expected FSD reliability to exceed a human driver in 2021. 2021-12-31 No Tesla did not demonstrate or deploy unsupervised driving that exceeded human reliability in 2021. Its current FSD remains supervised and SAE Level 2. No agreed public human-reliability benchmark was met by the deadline. Earnings call Tesla Q4 2020 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q4 2020 Earnings Call (Jan. 27, 2021); fool.com tesla.com ; nhtsa.gov 2021-01-27 FSD subscription Tesla expected to launch the FSD subscription in one or two months. 2021-03-27 No 2021-07-17 The monthly FSD subscription launched in July 2021, several months after the stated window. A revised deadline distinct from the earlier end-of-2020 forecast. Earnings call Tesla Q4 2020 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q4 2020 Earnings Call (Jan. 27, 2021) theverge.com 2021-01-27 Battery cells / 4680 Tesla expected to produce 100 GWh of its own cells in 2022 and have about 200 GWh of annual capacity at a roughly 30% utilization rate. 2022-12-31 No In December 2022 Tesla reported 868,000 4680 cells made in one week, enough for about 1,000 cars; that run-rate was only a few GWh per year, far below 100 GWh of production or 200 GWh of capacity. Earnings call Tesla Q4 2020 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q4 2020 Earnings Call (Jan. 27, 2021) x.com ; sec.gov 2021-01-27 Vehicle deliveries Tesla expected vehicle deliveries to grow more than 50% in 2021. 2021-12-31 Yes 2021-12-31 Tesla delivered 936,222 vehicles in 2021 versus 499,550 in 2020, growth of about 87%. Earnings call Tesla Q4 2020 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q4 2020 Earnings Call (Jan. 27, 2021) ir.tesla.com ; ir.tesla.com 2021-04-26 Model Y Model Y would probably be the world's best-selling vehicle of any kind in 2022. 2022-12-31 No 2023-12-31 Model Y did not become the world's best-selling vehicle until 2023. Earnings call Tesla Q1 2021 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q1 2021 Earnings Call (Apr. 26, 2021) jato.com 2021-04-26 Model S Deliveries of the refreshed Model S would begin in May 2021. 2021-05-31 No 2021-06-10 Tesla held the first Model S Plaid delivery event on June 10, 2021, after May. Earnings call Tesla Q1 2021 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q1 2021 Earnings Call (Apr. 26, 2021) reuters.com 2021-07-26 Battery cells / 4680 Tesla aimed to reach roughly 100 GWh annualized production of 4680 cells in 2022. 2022-12-31 No Tesla's December 2022 disclosure of 868,000 cells in one week implied only a few GWh per year, far below 100 GWh annualized. This forecast concerns the end-state annualized run-rate; P094 concerns total 2022 production and capacity. Earnings call Tesla Q2 2021 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q2 2021 Earnings Call (Jul. 26, 2021) x.com ; sec.gov 2021-07-26 Powerwall Tesla expected to reach an annualized production rate of one million Powerwalls in 2022. 2022-12-31 No One million current-size Powerwalls would represent at least 13.5 GWh. Tesla deployed only 6.5 GWh of all storage products combined in 2022, so the Powerwall-only run-rate was necessarily below the target. Earnings call Tesla Q2 2021 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q2 2021 Earnings Call (Jul. 26, 2021) tesla.com ; sec.gov 2021-08-19 Optimus Tesla would probably have a Tesla Bot prototype in 2022. 2022-12-31 Yes 2022-09-30 Tesla showed a walking Optimus prototype at AI Day 2022 on September 30, within the predicted year. Prototype demonstration counted; commercial usefulness was not part of this prediction. Public presentation Tesla AI Day youtube.com ; reuters.com reuters.com ; youtube.com 2022-01-26 Vehicle deliveries Tesla would comfortably grow deliveries more than 50% in 2022. 2022-12-31 No 2022-12-31 Tesla delivered 1.31 million vehicles in 2022, up 40% from 2021; production rose 47%. Neither measure exceeded 50%. Delivery-growth forecast assessed on Tesla's reported deliveries. Earnings call Tesla Q4 2021 earnings call Tesla, Inc., Q4 2021 Earnings Call (Jan. 26, 2022); Tesla, Inc., Q1 2022 Earnings Call (Apr. 20, 2022); reuters.com apnews.com ; ir.tesla.com

title: Molina Healthcare Set to Join S&P MidCap 400 and Construction Partners to Join S&P SmallCap 600
summary: S&P SmallCap 600 constituent Molina Healthcare Inc. (NYSE: MOH) will replace National Storage Affiliates Trust (NYSE: NSA) in the S&P MidCap 400, and Construction Partners Inc. (NASD: ROAD) will...
body_text: NEW YORK , July 16, 2026 / PRNewswire / -- S&P SmallCap 600 constituent Molina Healthcare Inc. (NYSE: MOH) will replace National Storage Affiliates Trust (NYSE: NSA) in the S&P MidCap 400, and Construction Partners Inc. (NASD: ROAD) will replace Molina Healthcare in the S&P SmallCap 600 effective prior to the opening of trading on Wednesday, July 22. S&P 500 constituent Public Storage (NYSE: PSA) is acquiring National Storage Affiliates Trust in a deal that is expected to be completed on or about that date pending final conditions. title: Rigel Appoints Board Member Alison L. Hannah, M.D. as Chief Medical Officer
body_text: Dr. Hannah has decades of oncology drug development experience and has served on Rigel's Board of Directors since 2021 She has resigned from Rigel's Board of Directors to join the company SOUTH SAN FRANCISCO, Calif. , July 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Rigel Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (Nasdaq: RIGL), a commercial stage biotechnology company focused on hematologic disorders and cancer, today announced the appointment of Alison L. Hannah, M.D. to the role of Executive Vice President and Chief Medical Officer. Dr. Hannah has resigned from Rigel's Board of Directors, effective July 1, 2026, in connection with her appointment. She succeeds Lisa Rojkjaer, M.D., as Chief Medical Officer. "Alison has been a valued member of Rigel's Board, and we are pleased to welcome her to the executive leadership team as Chief Medical Officer at an exciting time for Rigel. Her deep experience leading oncology clinical development and advancing investigational therapies through the regulatory process will be extremely valuable as we continue to advance our development pipeline, including R289 in lower-risk MDS, vepdegestrant in metastatic breast cancer and other potential opportunities," said Raul Rodriguez, Rigel's president and CEO. "On behalf of the entire Rigel team, I want to sincerely thank Lisa for her dedication and many contributions to the company." Rigel's leading pipeline asset, R2891, a potent and selective dual inhibitor of interleukin receptor-associated kinases 1 and 4 (IRAK1/4), continues to be advanced in its Phase 1b clinical study evaluating the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and preliminary efficacy in patients with relapsed or refractory lower-risk myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS). Enrollment in the dose expansion phase of the study is ongoing, and Rigel remains on track to complete enrollment and select the recommended Phase 2 dose for future clinical studies in the second half of 2026. The company continues to anticipate sharing preliminary data from the dose expansion phase of the study by the end of 2026. In addition, Rigel is progressing its evaluation of other potential indications to advance R289 and is planning to provide an update later this year. "I am excited to join Rigel at this important stage in the company's evolution. Having served on Rigel's Board, I have seen firsthand the strength of the team, the scientific rationale behind its programs and the opportunity to advance meaningful new therapies for patients with hematologic disorders and cancer," said Dr. Hannah. "I look forward to working closely with the leadership team to help guide the continued development of R289 and Rigel's broader clinical strategy, including the recent addition of vepdegestrant." About Dr. Hannah Alison L. Hannah, M. D. has been appointed Executive Vice President and Chief Medical Officer (CMO) of Rigel. She resigned from Rigel's Board of Directors, which she had served on since May 2021, in connection with her appointment as CMO. Previously, Dr. Hannah has held the roles of Chief Medical Officer of CytomX Therapeutics, where she oversaw clinical development of conditionally activated protein therapeutics, and Senior Medical Director at SUGEN, Inc. (acquired by Pharmacia & Upjohn, now Pfizer), where she had oversight of clinical development, clinical operations, and pharmacovigilance, specializing in the development of tyrosine kinase inhibitors, including sunitinib (SUTENT) approved for the treatment of kidney cancer and imatinib-refractory gastrointestinal stromal tumors. Dr. Hannah has served as a consultant to the pharmaceutical and biotechnology industry since 2000, directing the development of investigational cancer therapies. In this capacity, Dr. Hannah has successfully filed over 40 regulatory applications for first-in-human clinical testing and has played significant roles in the broad marketing approval of multiple anticancer therapeutics. Dr. Hannah began her career at Quintiles, a global contract research organization, where she specialized in overseeing early to registrational-stage oncology clinical trials. She has served since June 2015 on the Board of Directors for Neogenomics, a cancer diagnostic firm. Dr. Hannah received her B.A. in biochemistry and immunology from Harvard University and her M.D. from the University of St Andrews. About Rigel Rigel Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (Nasdaq: RIGL) is a biotechnology company dedicated to discovering, developing and providing novel therapies that significantly improve the lives of patients with hematologic disorders and cancer. Founded in 1996, Rigel is based in South San Francisco, California. For more information on Rigel, the Company's marketed products and pipeline of potential products, visit www.rigel.com . R289 is an investigational compound not approved by the FDA. Forward-Looking Statements This press release contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995 relating to, among other things, Rigel's clinical development plans and the potential of its product candidates, including R289; the anticipated timing of enrollment completion, dose selection and preliminary data from the ongoing Phase 1b clinical study of R289 in patients with relapsed or refractory lower-risk myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS); the evaluation of additional potential indications for R289; the advancement of Rigel's broader development pipeline, including vepdegestrant; and the expected contributions of Dr. Alison L. Hannah as Rigel's Chief Medical Officer. Any statements contained in this press release that are not statements of historical fact may be deemed to be forward-looking statements. Words such as "anticipates," "believes," "expects," "intends," "may," "plans," "potential," "will," and similar expressions are intended to identify such forward-looking statements. Forward-looking statements are based on Rigel's current beliefs, expectations and assumptions and involve risks and uncertainties that are difficult to predict and, in many cases, are beyond Rigel's control. title: ASE Announces FOCoS-Bridge with TSV; Latest Package Technology Reduces Power Loss by 3x for Next-Generation AI and HPC Applications
summary: This innovation improves performance by increasing bandwidth, shortening delivery paths, and enabling higher I/O density and better thermal dissipation. The integration of TSV boosts ASE’s VIPack™ FOCoS-Bridge capabilities, addressing the critical need for energy efficiency in emerging AI and high-performance computing applications.
body_text: SUNNYVALE, Calif., May 28, 2025 – Advanced Semiconductor Engineering, Inc. (ASE), a member of ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. (NYSE: ASX, TAIEX: 3711), today announced Fan-Out Chip-on-Substrate-Bridge (FOCoS-Bridge) with Through Silicon Via (TSV), propelling technology enablement for artificial intelligence (AI) and its pervasive impact on global life. Delivering critical performance improvements, ASE’s FOCoS-Bridge with TSV addresses growing demand for increased bandwidth by creating a shorter delivery path through TSV and enabling a higher I/O density and enhanced thermal dissipation. The integration of TSV expands ASE’s VIPack™ FOCoS-Bridge capabilities to deliver critical energy efficiency at a time when the need has never been greater across emerging AI and high-performance computing (HPC) applications. Future chiplet and high-bandwidth memory (HBM) integration will require higher interconnection densities to accommodate parallel higher data rate links and to preserve signal integrity. High-density interconnection is a key enabler of chiplet integration. AI and HPC power delivery requirements are becoming more complex and now necessitate advanced bridge chips with TSV features. The VIPack FOCoS-Bridge platform can be utilized for embedding passives and active dies, which can help improve power integrity and provide direct access for improved performance. “Artificial intelligence is increasingly integrated across a broad spectrum of applications—from intelligent manufacturing systems and autonomous vehicles to next-generation retail infrastructure and precision medical diagnostics—driving exponential growth in computational requirements and energy efficiency demands,” said Yin Chang, Executive Vice President at ASE. “Our introduction of the FOCoS-Bridge with TSV underscores ASE’s strategic commitment to supporting the AI ecosystem with advanced heterogeneous integration solutions. This innovation enhances our VIPack portfolio, offering a scalable, high-density packaging platform optimized for sustainable, high-performance computing architectures.” The expansion of ASE’s VIPack platform reflects the company’s strategic vision to provide a comprehensive, scalable ecosystem for sustainable, high-performance computing that meets the rigorous demands of emerging AI workloads. ASE’s FOCoS-Bridge with TSV can fulfill next-generation AI and HPC performance demands through heterogenous integration for high-power and high-bandwidth systems. Progress has been demonstrated using an 85mm x 85mm test vehicle comprised of two identical fan-out modules. Each module is made up of one ASIC chip and four HBM3 chips that are laterally interconnected with four TSV bridge chips as well as 10 integrated passive device chips. The TSV bridge chips provide a new shorter vertical path for power delivery in conjunction with traditional lateral signal connections. The TSV and passive devices are embedded and interconnected using three redistribution layers (RDLs) with 5µm line and space. When compared to FOCoS-Bridge, the resistance and inductance of FOCoS-Bridge TSV are significantly reduced by 72% and 50%, respectively. “The growing demands of HPC and AI applications are accelerating the need for greater computational performance, and ASE’s FOCoS-Bridge capabilities enable seamless integration of SoCs and chiplets with high-bandwidth memory,” said Teck Lee, Director of R&D at ASE. “By incorporating TSV, FOCoS-Bridge enhances compute and energy efficiency, and elevates our advanced packaging portfolio to the next level.” FOCoS-Bridge technology has already demonstrated its ability to address higher bandwidth and faster data transfer rates in AI and HPC applications. It leverages the advantages of highly integrated fan-out structures to overcome the limitations of traditional electrical interconnects, and enables high-speed, low-latency, and energy-efficient data communication between processors, accelerators, and memory modules. While establishing the foundation for embedding passives and active chips in the fan-out package, FOCoS-Bridge also provides options of decoupling capacitor integration for power delivery optimization and active dies for interconnection between to certain functions, such as memory, I/O, and more. “ASE is strategically positioned at the forefront of the industry as a premier provider of advanced packaging solutions for high-power AI and high-performance computing applications,” said Charles Lee, Director of Engineering and Technical Promotion at ASE. “Our strength lies in our ability to deliver innovative technologies that address customers’ evolving needs in a rapidly advancing market.” ASE will participate at ECTC 2025 in Dallas, May 27-30, 2025, with an exhibition showcasing our VIPack technologies, while delivering a suite of technologist presentations and panelist opinion across the conference program. title: Stripe for Hotels: Why It Often Fails and What to Use Instead
summary: Stripe works well for e-commerce. For hotels and tour operators in emerging markets, it's a different story. Here's what actually happens — and what to use instead.
body_text: Stripe is the first place most people look when they want to start accepting card payments online. It's well-known, the documentation is good, and it works seamlessly for e-commerce businesses in the US and Europe. For a lot of hotels, tour operators, and activity providers in Asia, Africa, and Latin America, it is either not available in their country, or it doesn't well. The most common problem is account freezes. Stripe classifies tourism as high-risk, which means your account can be suspended - sometimes without warning - if you process too many refunds, receive chargebacks, or simply trigger their fraud filters. For a hotel that relies on card payments to collect deposits and confirm bookings, a frozen account is an immediate cash flow crisis. Stripe operates in around 45 countries. If you're running a property in Kenya, Bolivia, Indonesia, or most of West Africa, you can't create a Stripe account at all. If you were to use a registered business address in another country, there are complications with payouts and tax. For hotels that do get Stripe working, American Express is often the next issue. Stripe supports American Express in theory, but in practice a significant number of American Express transactions decline when processed through Stripe accounts in South America, Africa, and Asia. For properties that host a lot of US and European travellers, who disproportionately carry American Express, this means turning away payments from some of your highest-spending guests. Stripe lacks a lot of features for tourism businesses. It's built for e-commerce - recurring subscriptions, online storefronts, marketplaces. It has no way to charge the virtual credit cards that OTAs like Booking.com and Expedia send through, and no mechanism for sending a payment request over WhatsApp. These are everyday workflows for a hotel. PayPal has most of the same problems, plus fees that compound badly on international transactions. A tour operator in Vietnam paying PayPal's exchange rate markup can lose dollars per transaction before the standard fee even kicks in. The platforms that tend to work for tourism businesses in emerging markets are purpose-built for the use case. Tab, for example, supports card acceptance in markets where Stripe and PayPal don't operate, accepts American Express, doesn't freeze accounts based on tourism industry classification, and is built around the workflows that hotels and tour operators actually use - payment links, advance deposits, OTA virtual card charging, and an embeddable booking widget for direct bookings. The fee structure is also straightforward: 2.9% plus $1 for advance bookings, 2.9% for in-person payments, with free payouts to any bank account in 140+ currencies every week. No monthly fees, no setup costs, no hardware. Disclosure: Availability, onboarding requirements, and payment-workflow support vary by country, business model, and provider. Information in this article is accurate as of May 18, 2026. Sources: Stripe global availability, Stripe restricted-business guidance, Stripe’s hotel payment processing guide, Booking.com and Expedia documentation on OTA payment flows.

title: When to Start Potty Training: A Pediatrician's Guide to Readiness Signs
summary: Wondering when to start potty training? A pediatrician explains the readiness signs to watch for, the typical age range, how to begin, and when to call your doctor.
body_text: Most children are ready to start potty training between 18 and 36 months. The right time depends on your child's signs, not their birthday. The American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) tells parents to watch for physical, behavioral, and cognitive readiness cues, and to wait until those cues show up. Readiness matters more than age. "Most parents come in worried they are starting too late. In our experience, the family that waits for true readiness almost always has an easier time than the family that pushes by the calendar." Blueberry Pediatrics Care Team Key Takeaways Readiness comes before age. The AAP says children should not be pushed to start until they are physically, behaviorally, and developmentally ready. Most kids start between 18 and 36 months. The U.S. average is between 2 and 3 years old. About 6 in 10 children are trained by age 3, and nearly all are trained by age 4. Intensive training before 27 months does not get most kids trained any faster. Call your pediatrician for painful constipation, stool withholding, no progress by age 4, or regression with pain, fever, or unusual thirst. Not sure if your child is ready, or worried about a recent setback? Talk to a Blueberry pediatrician What Age Should You Start Potty Training? Most parents start between 18 and 36 months. The U.S. average start is between ages 2 and 3, according to HealthyChildren.org, the parent-facing site of the American Academy of Pediatrics. The right age depends much more on your child's readiness than on a calendar number. The Typical Age Range (18 to 36 Months) A few primary-source numbers help set realistic expectations: The average age of first toilet-training success is about 27.7 months, and steady daytime success comes around 28.5 months. About 6 in 10 children are trained by age 3, and nearly all by age 4. These are averages. The normal range is wide. If your 2-year-old is not interested yet, or your 3-year-old is still working on it, you are well inside normal. Why Readiness Matters More Than Age The body and the brain need to be ready before potty training can stick: Sphincter control (the muscle control needed to hold pee and poop) usually is not in place before 18 months. Cognitive readiness, the ability to connect the inner "I need to go" feeling with using the potty, usually shows up after the second birthday. Intensive training before 27 months does not lead to faster completion. If your child shows several readiness signs, you can start. If not, wait a few weeks and try again. Pushing a child who is not ready usually leads to power struggles, accidents, and constipation, not faster training. Signs Your Child Is Ready to Potty Train Readiness shows up in three areas: physical, behavioral, and cognitive. No child needs every sign. Look for a cluster of cues across all three areas. The AAP emphasizes that readiness can spread out and rarely arrives all at once. Physical Readiness Signs Stays dry for at least 2 hours at a stretch, or wakes up dry from naps. This is a sign the bladder is maturing. Walks easily to the potty and sits down steadily. Can pull pants and underwear up and down. Shows the "about to go" tells: grunting, squatting, freezing, a red face, or tugging at the diaper. Has regular, soft, formed bowel movements on a roughly predictable schedule. Behavioral Readiness Signs Does not like the feeling of a wet or dirty diaper, and may ask to be changed. Shows interest in the toilet, in siblings or parents using it, or in "big kid" skills. Wants to do things "myself" and takes pride in small accomplishments. Can follow simple instructions and cooperate with a short routine. Cognitive and Language Readiness Signs Connects the inner feeling of a full bladder or rectum with the act of going. Has words or signs for pee, poop, and the potty, and can tell you before or during going. Can remember where they are headed and ignore distractions on the way. Follows the steps of a short sequence: pants down, sit, wipe, flush, hands. If most of these are in place, your child is probably ready. If only one or two are showing up, it is okay to wait. The AAP frames the whole process as child-led, not parent-led. How to Start Potty Training: Step-by-Step Here is a simple plan, based on HealthyChildren.org. You do not need fancy gear or a chart full of stickers. You need a routine, neutral words, and patience. Pick your words. Choose simple, family-friendly words for body parts, pee, and poop. Avoid words like "dirty" or "stinky." Neutral words keep shame out of the routine. Get a potty chair. A small, child-sized seat with a removable container works well. Your child's feet should reach the floor. Stable footing helps with control. Build a routine. Have your child sit on the potty at predictable times: first thing in the morning, after meals, and before bath. A short book can make potty time feel calm and positive. Teach the cues. Name the cues out loud the moment you see them. "Looks like you are doing the potty dance. Let's try the potty." This helps your child link the body feeling to the action. Praise effort, not just success. Steady, low-key praise works better than big rewards. Model it. Let your child watch a parent or older sibling use the toilet and wash hands. Toddlers learn by copying. Hand over control. Talk about pee and poop as your child's job, not yours. The AAP calls this "toilet mastery." Kids who feel in charge stay more motivated. Never punish accidents. The AAP is clear: pushing, shaming, or punishing for accidents backfires. Take a break of a few weeks if the process feels stuck. Common Potty Training Methods You will hear about a lot of methods. Most fall into two camps: a fast, intensive approach, or a slow, child-led approach. Only the gradual approach has outcome data from peer-reviewed studies. The 3-Day Method The 3-day method is an intensive, parent-led approach. You clear your calendar, put your child in underwear, and stay home for a few days of focused practice, hourly potty visits, and lots of fluids. It can work for a child who is already showing clear readiness signs and who is comfortable with the parent's full attention for several days. No primary source supports a fixed 3-day timeline, and intensive training before 27 months does not give children a head start. If you try this approach, do not start before your child shows steady readiness, and be ready to pause if your child becomes upset or starts withholding. The Child-Led (Gradual) Method The child-led method is the AAP-aligned default, and it has the strongest track record in pediatric research. Parents follow the child's readiness for each step instead of pushing a timeline: Introduce the potty chair when your child is around 18 to 24 months and curious. Move on to sitting in clothes, then with the diaper off, only when your child is comfortable. Try regular pants once your child uses the potty reliably for several days. Take a break if your child resists, then try again in a few weeks. This route is slower at the start, but outcomes are strong, and power struggles and constipation are less common. Potty Training Boys vs. Girls: What's Different? On average, boys finish potty training about 6 months later than girls (HealthyChildren.org). The AAP is careful with this number. "Gender itself has little to do with how early or late a child becomes fully toilet-trained," the AAP writes. Differences in activity level and overall readiness timing matter more than sex. A few practical tips: Many boys find it easier to sit for both pee and poop first, then switch to standing for pee once the basics are solid. A foot-supported potty chair helps with both. Keep individual readiness as your main signal. A ready boy will train faster than a not-ready girl. Do not start earlier for a girl or wait longer for a boy just because of sex. Watch your individual child. Troubleshooting Common Potty Training Problems Even with a smooth start, almost every family hits a few bumps. Most are normal and pass on their own. A few need a quick check-in with your pediatrician. Accidents and Regression Accidents are normal during and after potty training. HealthyChildren.org notes that accidents "sometimes continue for months after the toilet training process appears complete, even when a child is three or four years old." This is part of the process, not failure. Regression, where a previously trained child starts having accidents again or asks for diapers back, often follows a change at home: a new baby, a move, a new caregiver or preschool, illness, or family stress. It can also signal a medical cause, especially a urinary tract infection (UTI) or constipation. Rule out a medical cause first When a previously trained child regresses, have the pediatrician check for a physical cause before changing your routine. Regression can signal an infection or another condition that needs treatment. Once a medical cause is ruled out, react calmly. Walk back to the basics: regular potty sits, praise for effort, no punishment, and a steady routine for a few weeks. Refusal and Power Struggles Many toddlers go through a stage of refusing the potty. They are testing control, not failing. If you push, you can turn refusal into constipation. "Holding back stools because of power struggles is the most common cause of recurrent constipation in children, most often occurring during toilet training," HealthyChildren.org reports. Up to 1 in 5 children show stool toileting refusal at some point. For most, it passes; for about one in four of those, a pediatrician's help is useful. Two terms to know: Stool withholding is when a child holds in poop on purpose, often to avoid a painful poop or to keep control. Constipation means hard, dry, or painful poops (the hardness matters more than how often). If refusal is steady, the simplest plan is to step back. Put your child back in diapers or pull-ups for a few weeks, drop the potty conversation, and try again later. A break is not a defeat. It is good pediatric practice. (Learn more in our guide to toddler constipation and what green poop means .) Nighttime Training and Bedwetting Nighttime dryness comes later than daytime dryness, and on its own timeline. Many kids are dry during the day for months, or even a year, before they are reliably dry at night. About 1 in 5 children still wet the bed at age 5 (HealthyChildren.org). That is usually normal, and the AAP notes that "bedwetting almost always goes away on its own." Doctors only call it "nocturnal enuresis" (the medical word for bedwetting) when it continues beyond age 5. For most kids, nighttime training is about waiting, not training. Use a waterproof mattress cover, keep nighttime calm and matter-of-fact, and skip the punishment. Call your pediatrician if bedwetting is new after 6 months of dry nights, painful, or paired with increased thirst, increased urination, or burning. When to Talk to Your Pediatrician Most potty training questions ("Is this normal?" or "Why is my child suddenly having accidents?") are great for a quick telehealth visit. A few situations need an in-person check. Call your pediatrician if: Your child has painful constipation or is holding in poop. An in-person exam may be needed to check for a stool impaction. Your child has shown no potty training progress by age 4, or shows no readiness signs well past age 3. A previously trained child suddenly starts having accidents, especially with pain, fever, blood in the urine, or unusual thirst or urination. These can point to a UTI or another condition that needs care. Bedwetting starts up again after 6 or more months of dry nights, or comes with daytime symptoms. In our telehealth visits, the most common parent questions are how to tell if a child is really ready, and what to do when a child who was doing well suddenly starts having accidents. Both are well suited to a quick virtual visit. Suspected constipation causing pain, or a possible UTI, needs an in-person exam. Worried about constipation, regression, or a refusal that is lasting weeks? Message a Blueberry pediatrician now Frequently Asked Questions Does the 3-day method really work? It can work for a child who already shows clear readiness signs, but there is no fixed timeline. Intensive training before 27 months does not lead to faster completion than the gradual approach. How is potty training boys different from girls? Boys average about 6 months later than girls, but the AAP says individual readiness matters far more than sex. Many boys do well sitting for both pee and poop first, then switching to standing later. See our pediatrician's guide to potty training boys for step-by-step tips. What do I do about accidents and regression? Accidents are normal for months after "finished" training. If a previously trained child starts having accidents again, have your pediatrician rule out a UTI or constipation first, then walk back to a calm, basic routine. A sudden behavior shift can also overlap with common toddler sleep regressions . What if my child refuses to use the potty? Refusal is common. Do not push or punish, which can turn into stool withholding and constipation. Take a break of a few weeks and try again. When should my child be night-trained, and what about bedwetting? Nighttime dryness comes later than daytime, on its own clock. About 1 in 5 children still wet the bed at age 5, which is usually normal. It almost always resolves on its own. Can you start potty training too early? Before about 18 months, the body usually cannot control elimination yet. Intensive training before 27 months gives no proven head start. Is it normal for my child not to be potty trained by age 3? Yes. About 4 in 10 children are still potty training at age 3. Nearly all are trained by age 4. The Surprising Side Effects of Ambien You Should Know About
summary: Discover the surprising effects of Ambien beyond sleep. Learn about its unexpected side effects and make informed choices for better health and well-being.
body_text: Explore the surprising side effects of Ambien and understand how this sleep aid can paradoxically worsen insomnia and provoke other unexpected reactions. Dr. Shiyan Yeo, Internal Medicine Physician, Sleep Medicine Expert: “Ambien may impair coordination, memory, and alertness even after waking—especially if not timed properly.” Take the first step towards improving your sleep with Sleep Reset. Start by taking our sleep quiz , enabling us to pinpoint your key issues. Following the quiz, opt to work with your personal sleep coach and gain access to our dedicated sleep program. It's a proactive approach to address sleep concerns without the risks associated with medications like Ambien. Sleeping pills vs. Sleep Reset Insomnia and Sleep Disturbances Ironically, those prescribed Ambien to alleviate sleep disturbances may find themselves in a paradox. Instead of providing relief, this medication has the potential to intensify symptoms, turning peaceful night's slumbers into bouts of wakefulness and restlessness. Patients seek Ambien for its sleep-inducing properties, but sometimes it backfires, inducing a worsening spiral of insomnia. Rather than improving sleep quality, it exacerbates the very condition it was meant to mitigate, catching patients in an unforgiving cycle of disturbed sleep. The Paradoxical Effect of Ambien Ambien, known for inducing sleep in insomnia sufferers , can introduce a paradoxical effect. This counterintuitive reaction amplifies restless and agitation, the exact symptoms individuals seek to eliminate with Ambien use. Ambien may have a counterproductive effect leading to heightened restlessness and aggravated insomnia, necessitating medication adjustments. Notably, this paradoxical outcome can be particularly disruptive for patients. Instead of improving sleep patterns, it can deteriorate them, leading to longer, more severely restless nights. It's crucial to understand the potentially backfiring impact of Ambien. Unforeseen repercussions, such as increased agitation and insomnia, can necessitate changes in a patient's medication regimen. Worsening of Sleep Quality While intended as a sleep aid, Ambien paradoxically may degrade sleep quality over time. Chronic use can lead to fragmented sleep, frequent awakenings, and decreased slow-wave sleep, disrupting restorative sleep phases. Ambien's negative impact on sleep quality is significant. Rebound insomnia, a condition where sleep disturbances are worse after stopping medication, is common. This effect raises fresh questions about the efficacy of medication-assisted sleeping. Nightmares and Confusion Chilling nightmares can be a disturbing aftermath of Ambien use. These vivid, distressing dreams often disrupt sleep rather than promote it, adding a brutal irony to your quest for rest. Ambien-induced disorientation is another unnerving side effect. When users awaken at night, they often experience profound confusion, making even the most familiar environments seem strange and bewildering. Cognitive Impairment Dr. Michael Grandner, Sleep Expert, Professor of Neuroscience and Physiological Sciences: “Some people experience complex behaviors like sleep-eating or even sleep-driving. These risks should never be ignored.” Ambien's stealthy impact on cerebral performance can manifest as memory deficits and hindered decision-making. Ambien use, aside from initiating sleep, brings forth cognitive risks, subtly impairing crucial mental processes. Memory Problems Ambien, known generically as zolpidem tartrate, poses an increasing risk of memory problems , which can be disconcerting for many users. This potential side effect is often referred to as 'Ambien Amnesia,' characterizing disruptions in forming and recalling memories while under the influence of the medication. Amnesia episodes due to Ambien usually occur if users do not sleep immediately after taking the drug. Complete blackouts and inability to remember actions performed while on the medication may occur. Incorrect or reduced dosage can alleviate this side effect, while prolonged misuse may result in sustained memory impairment. Delirium or temporary periods of disorientation, delusion, or hallucinations may accompany memory problems. Impaired Judgment and Decision-Making One prominent cognitive side effect of Ambien can be impaired judgment and decision-making, leading to surprising and sometimes dangerous consequences. This consequence is particularly concerning as it can distort a patient's rationality or cognitive performance, often without their awareness. Unexpected impulsive behavior Decreased problem-solving skills Risk-taking behavior or poor risk assessment skills Difficulty in making sound judgments Impaired motor skills, potentially leading to accidents. Addiction and Dependence Ambien, intended for short-term relief from insomnia, can ironically become a source of substantial reliance. The slow, often unnoticed, slide into dependency can pivot a solution into a potential problem. Early signs of addiction range from escalating dosage without a doctor's guidance to increasing preoccupation with the drug. Unmasking these signs can be instrumental in averting the subtle, insidious creep of Ambien addiction. Tolerance and Increased Dosage The more you consume Ambien, the more your body builds a tolerance towards it. This increased tolerance often leads to a higher dosage, escalating the scale of usage, subsequently increasing potential risks. Amplified tolerance to the effects of the drugs over time. Increased dosage to achieve desired sleep results. Heightened dependence due to prolonged usage. Augmented risk of adverse side effects. Possible escalation towards misuse and addiction. Withdrawal Symptoms Facing sudden withdrawal from Ambien can trigger a cascade of ripple effects. Patients may experience rebound insomnia, anxiety, tremors, and, quite rarely, even seizures, highlighting the importance of medical supervision during dosage reduction. Being able to pinpoint symptoms of Ambien withdrawal contributes significantly to effective management. Symptoms can encompass physical discomfort, emotional unsteadiness, or sleep disturbances, with individuals often experiencing more intense insomnia than prior to medication use. Behavioral Changes Despite its intended use to facilitate sleep, Ambien can notably exhibit personality alterations and provoke unpredictable behaviors. In essence, a calm and collective person can unexpectedly become agitated and behave erratically. Aggression, irritability, and unpredictable actions are some of the veiled side effects of Ambien. In some individuals, these alterations can escalate quickly, leading to critical mental health issues that extend well beyond a disturbed night's sleep. Mood Swings and Emotional Instability Ambien can precipitate unsettling emotional upheavals, causing users to grapple with fluctuating temperaments and moods. This volatility may often leave the individual as well as those around them in a state of constant unease. Further, the drug's emotional whirl may exacerbate or usher in conditions like depression or anxiety. These emotional disturbances, though they seem subtle initially, can burgeon into major issues impacting overall well-being and quality of life. Start Sleeping Better With Sleep Reset Today! Our free sleep quiz can help you identify the underlying causes of your sleep problems, so you can find the best solution for you. Our program does not rely on harmful pills, melatonin or supplements – which means no grogginess, dependency, or long-term health risks. Instead of relying on quick fixes, we use proven techniques to address the root causes of your sleep issues and give you the long-term tools to manage your sleep. Our dedicated sleep coach will help you via daily text to provide accountability, support, and guidance. Try more natural sleep aids like magnesium or l-theanine , but keep in mind that these substances might also have side effects albeit fewer than sleeping pills.
